scale_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft the initial sections of our company employee handbook. Before starting, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: company legal name, state(s)/countries where we employ people, current PTO policy details (accrual rules, carryover, holidays observed), remote/hybrid work expectations, code of conduct or anti-harassment stance, equity plan basics (vesting schedule, plan name if any), and any existing policy docs I want you to incorporate rather than draft from scratch.

Using this information, draft clear, plain-language sections covering: (1) Welcome/company overview, (2) Employment basics (at-will status if applicable, classification), (3) Code of conduct and anti-harassment policy, (4) PTO, holidays, and leave policies, (5) Remote/hybrid work policy, (6) Equity overview (high-level, non-legal explanation pointing employees to their individual grant docs for specifics), (7) Compensation and benefits overview, (8) Workplace safety and reporting procedures, and (9) Acknowledgment/signature section. Write each section in a shared document (e.g., Google Doc or Notion page) organized with clear headings so it can be reviewed and edited easily.

Flag any section where legal review is advisable (e.g., at-will language, leave compliance, anti-harassment policy) with an inline note such as "[LEGAL REVIEW SUGGESTED]" rather than asserting compliance yourself, since legal accuracy varies by jurisdiction and this remains a human step.

When done, report back: the document link or location, a list of sections completed, any sections left as placeholders pending missing information from me, and all flagged legal-review notes. Do not publish, distribute, or announce the handbook to employees — this draft is for internal review only, and finalizing/publishing must stop for human sign-off.

scale_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me customize the policy sections of our employee handbook before it goes to leadership for approval. This is a drafting/preparation task only — final policy terms must be decided and approved by leadership.

First, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: company name, state/country of incorporation and primary work locations, headcount, PTO philosophy (accrual vs. unlimited, current amounts if any), remote/hybrid/in-office policy, equity plan basics (option pool, vesting schedule, cliff), code of conduct concerns specific to our industry, and any existing draft handbook or template we've used before.

Using that information, draft customized policy text for each core section: PTO and holidays, code of conduct, remote/hybrid work rules, and equity/vesting provisions. For each section:
- Write clear, plain-language policy text tailored to the inputs I gave you.
- Flag any spot where leadership needs to make an explicit decision (e.g., exact PTO days, vesting cliff length, remote-work eligibility rules) with a clearly marked placeholder like [DECISION NEEDED: ...].
- Note any obvious legal/compliance considerations (e.g., state-mandated leave, at-will employment language) as flags for legal review, not as finalized text.

Compile all sections into a single organized draft document, with a summary list at the top of every open decision point that still needs leadership input.

When the draft is ready, present it to me along with the decision list and stop for human sign-off — do not finalize wording, publish, distribute, or treat any placeholder as approved. My job afterward is to review, make the final calls with leadership, and approve the finished language.

scale_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the employee handbook draft for employment-law legal review before publication. This is a policy-gate step: you must assemble everything needed for an attorney to review, but you must NOT approve, sign, accept, or publish the handbook yourself — legal sign-off is required from a human attorney.

First, ask me for: (1) the current draft of the employee handbook (file or doc link), (2) the jurisdiction(s)/states or countries where we have employees, (3) the name and contact (email) of the employment attorney or law firm doing the review, and (4) any prior review notes or open questions I already have.

Once you have these, please:
1. Compile a clean, clearly-labeled copy of the full handbook draft (policies, PTO, conduct, remote work, equity sections) suitable for attorney review, with section numbers for easy reference.
2. Draft a concise cover email to the attorney/law firm requesting a compliance review, listing our jurisdictions, our target publish date, and specific areas of concern (e.g., PTO accrual rules, remote work across state lines, equity disclosures).
3. Create a tracking checklist noting: date sent, reviewer, expected turnaround, and a status field set to 'awaiting attorney feedback.'
4. Since this is an async, third-party-dependent step, note in the checklist that you cannot force a response — periodically check for a reply (e.g., check email or shared doc comments) and flag me when feedback arrives, but do not proceed to publish or apply any legal changes without my explicit review.

When the attorney's feedback arrives, prepare a redlined summary of requested changes and a revised draft incorporating them, but stop for human sign-off before finalizing or publishing — I must personally confirm the attorney's approval before anything goes live.

Report back with: the compiled draft, the cover email text, the tracking checklist, and current review status.

scale_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me publish our finished employee handbook content into {{vendor}}, our project-management workspace tool, as a structured set of pages. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: the finalized handbook text/draft (or its file location), the {{vendor}} workspace or space where it should live, the desired page hierarchy (e.g., a parent 'Employee Handbook' page with child pages for Conduct, PTO, Remote Work, Equity, and other policies), and confirmation that you have configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s API or interface.

Once you have the content, use your configured credentials to connect to {{vendor}} and prepare (but do not finalize) the page structure: draft the parent handbook page and each policy section as its own sub-page, formatted with clear headings matching our source document, preserving section order and any tables or lists. Where {{vendor}} supports it via its documented API, prepare the create-page operations as a batch so they can be reviewed before execution; otherwise draft the exact content and structure to be entered manually.

Do not publish, save, or apply any changes yet. Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, compile a clear preview: the full page tree, page titles, and content summaries for each section, plus any warnings about formatting that may not translate perfectly (e.g., complex tables). Present this preview along with the exact steps you would take to publish once approved.

After preparing this, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: (1) the proposed page structure and locations in {{vendor}}, (2) the full draft content or a link/reference to it, (3) any formatting risks or open questions, and (4) confirmation that no pages have been created yet and you are awaiting my explicit approval to proceed.

scale_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me announce our new employee handbook to the team via {{vendor}}, our email platform. Before drafting, ask me for: (1) the final handbook link or file location, (2) the list or distribution group of team recipients, (3) the sender inbox/address to send from, and (4) any key highlights I want called out (e.g., new PTO policy, remote work rules, equity plan updates, effective date).

Once you have this, draft a clear, warm announcement email in my voice that: states the handbook is now official, links to it, summarizes the major sections (policies, PTO, conduct, remote work, equity), notes the effective date, and tells employees who to contact with questions. Use {{vendor}}'s documented connection or public API to prepare the message in the configured inbox as a draft — do not send it yet.

Show me the full draft (subject line, body, recipient list, sender address) exactly as it will be sent through {{vendor}}. Then stop for human sign-off — do not send, submit, or approve the send action yourself. Wait for my explicit confirmation.

Once I approve, send the message using {{vendor}}'s send-message API or dashboard equivalent, and confirm back to me with the send timestamp, the recipient count, and the message ID or delivery confirmation returned by {{vendor}}. If sending fails or bounces occur, report the exact error and pause for my next instruction rather than retrying automatically.
